lines.text: A single spark in a midnight bakery ignited an inferno so ferocious, it melted the lead roof of Saint Paul's Cathedral.
Fueled by fierce eastern winds, the firestorm tore through London's overcrowded timber-framed streets, turning entire neighborhoods to ash.
Panic-stricken citizens crowded the River Thames in rowboats, watching four hundred streets vanish into a glowing wall of fire.
Old Saint Paul's Cathedral collapsed as six acres of lead roof melted into molten streams cascading down the city hills.
Only by detonating gunpowder charges to blow up entire rows of houses was the devastating inferno finally halted.
From London's smoking ashes rose Sir Christopher Wren's stone masterpiece. Subscribe to Beyond History for more.
